messages:
maya: quick sync — noticed p99 tail spikes on a handful of pods when prefetch rate climbs and batch assembly stalls. thinking a 'queue-shepherd' fallback: prefer KV-hit requests + kernel-hint routing before issuing broad soft-429s. anyone seen similar?

arjun: saw this yesterday on canary — when kernel v2.4 changed memcpy path we got more microbatch assembly delay. KV-hit ratio drops -> fewer prefix cache saves -> longer seqs, bigger kernels. :grimacing:

sam: profiler snapshot from one bad pod earlier (trimmed):
```
kernel_dispatch memcpy: 18.4ms
attention_kernel v2.4: 11.2ms
batch_assembler wait: 32.1ms
kv_lookup + merge: 2.3ms (hit 43%)
```
p99 latency ~ 290ms vs baseline 180ms.

laura: timeline — that memcpy tweak landed with the kernel selection heuristic that prefers v2.4 for >1024 tokens. might be a bad heuristic when queue assembly has jitter.

maya: exactly. my proposal:
- admission: maintain per-queue token_budget target (soft) and a KV-hit weight.
- on enqueue, tag request with kv_hit_prob (from fast local lookup) and seq_len_est.
- queue-shepherd prioritizes scheduling for high kv_hit_prob and short seq_len_est; low-priority requests may be deferred to microbatch path rather than soft-429.
- fallback: if queues exceed soft limit for Xs, emit soft-429s only for lowest-priority cohort.

arjun: +1. also add kernel hint to batch header so the batcher can pick a fast kernel variant if >80% of items prefer it. saves kernel-switch overhead.

sam: quick sketch of scoring function I used in simulation:
```
score = w_kv * kv_hit_prob - w_len * (seq_len_est/1024) - w_wait * queue_wait_s
if score < throttle_threshold -> send to microbatch queue
else -> normal fast-path
```
We simulated with w_kv=2, w_len=1.5, w_wait=1. results: 18% fewer soft-429s, p99 down 12%.

laura: question: how do we get kv_hit_prob cheaply? we can't always check distributed cache on enqueue.

maya: use local LRU shadow-probe — check prefix trie / small bloom + recent local k/v stats. cheap approximate probability. we already ship a small per-worker perf cache.

arjun: also track per-worker recent kernel latency vector; if a kernel variant spikes, shepherd will bias away from that kernel for new batches.

ci-bot: CI perf test ran against branch queue-shepherd-heuristic: 4/5 regression tests passed, perf bucketing shows p95 stable, p99 improved on sim. Full results: https://ci.company/12345

sam: one gotcha — microbatch path needs to preserve streaming behavior where callers expect partial tokens. if we coalesce too aggressively we break streaming SLOs.

maya: agreed. microbatch path only for non-streaming or very short streaming windows; we need a max-coalesced-latency knob.

laura: ops question — what are the alerting thresholds? if we move to cohorted soft-429s, we should add counting metrics: soft429_by_cohort, admitted_by_kernel_hint, kv_prefetch_hitrate_local.

maya: good call. action items:
- arjun: prototype kernel-hint header + scoring in batcher (owner) — due EOD Wed
- sam: extend simulation with streaming-aware microbatch constraints and run p99 sims — due Thu
- laura: add metric names + dashboards + alert thresholds draft — due Fri
- maya: draft rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with kill-switch based on soft429 spike and p99 regressions — due Mon

arjun: pushing prototype branch now. small note: will add a feature flag queue_shepherd.enabled and a toggle for scoring weights.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued for staging from arjun/queue-shepherd-heuristic — status: pending

sam: quick stat from a local sim after adjusting w_kv to 2.5: soft-429s reduced 22%, median unchanged, p99 improved ~14%.

laura: marking this as meeting followup. can we include an A/B test that routes by user-tier? enterprise tenants get kv-priority by default.

maya: yes — include tier override in scoring. ok team, sync done. :thumbsup: will post a short PR checklist and link to ci results.

ci-bot: perf artifact uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/queue-shepherd/1729993333/ — contains traces and scorer sim logs.

laura: also add runbook note: if kernel_selection_flap occurs (>5 kernel swaps/min on a worker) auto-disable kernel hinting for that worker.

maya: noted. thanks everyone.
